references.text: The priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven—the same principle of the priest's atoning act for the congregation
The priest shall make atonement for him for his sin, and he shall be forgiven—a parallel formula for atonement and forgiveness
Concerns atonement for unintentional sin (שְׁגָגָה) and forgiveness
Continuation of the same text—the entire assembly of Israel shall be forgiven because it was an unintentional sin
The priest shall make atonement for the one who sins through error—the same theme of unintentional sin and atonement
A fire offering (אִשֶּׁה) to the Lord with a pleasing aroma—background for the concept of fire offerings
Ὃ προσφέρει ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων—the high priest offers sacrifice for the sins of the people committed in ignorance
The high priest can make allowance for those who are ignorant and erring, and must offer sacrifice for the people's sins as well as his own
On this day atonement shall be made for you, so that you may be cleansed from all your sins—the Day of Atonement
